copies.headline: Adam Is 6-0 And Barely Needed Luck
copies.body: Nothing to argue with here. Adam is 6-0, leads the league at 150.9 per game, and his all-play is 59-7 — 89 percent, best in the league, meaning he'd be winning against almost anyone on any given Sunday. The +0.6 luck is a rounding error on a résumé built entirely on scoring. His season low is 132.7, which is most teams' ceiling. Draft-night roster graded 89, second-best, and it projects 137 a week going forward, also first. The career wins leader is just doing the thing again. John gets him in Week 7.

copies.headline: John's Scoring Is Real, His Record Isn't
copies.body: John is 3-3 with the second-best scoring average in the league at 128.5 and a 41-25 all-play, which is the polite way of saying he's been beaten by the schedule, not by his opponents. Luck sits at -0.7 wins. The last three weeks — 135.7, 172.7, then a 100.1 faceplant — tell you the range, but 23-10 all-play over that stretch says the floor is fine. The draft night roster graded 80, T-9th, and he's outrun it anyway. Puka Nacua projects 25. Week 7 brings Adam.

copies.headline: 2-4 Is A Clerical Error
copies.body: Christian is 2-4 with the 4th-best scoring average in the league at 127.7 and an all-play mark of 39-27, which is the polite way of saying he's been mugged. Luck sits at -1.5 wins, 783.9 points against is the 11th-fewest, and the math isn't subtle. The draft-night roster graded T-2nd at 89, and it still looks the part: Lamb, Kittle, Chase Brown, 125 a week projected, 3rd of 12. He won last week. Grant's next, and 122 should be plenty.

copies.headline: Logan's 2-4 Lies, The Scoring Doesn't
copies.body: The dress jokes can wait. Logan is 2-4, but he's taken 836.6 points against — fewest-favorable draw in the league at 12th of 12 — and sits at -1.5 wins versus expected. His all-play is 38-28, 5th of 12, and over the last three weeks it's 25-8, 2nd of 12, with 112.9, 142.3 and 152.5 on the board. Justin Jefferson, Tetairoa McMillan and Jaylen Warren are finally cashing. He jumped six spots for a reason. Week 7 projects 127 against Isaac. The 2-4 is a clerical error.

copies.headline: Leif Is Outrunning His Own Roster
copies.body: Leif is 4-2 with the 3rd-best scoring average in the league at 128.4, and the all-play backs it up — 40-26, 61%, 3rd of 12. That's earned, not lucky, with a +0.4 luck number that's basically neutral. The problem is everything underneath. His draft night roster graded 80, 12th of 12, and the current group projects for roughly 106 a week, 11th of 12. Week 4's 82.8 was the preview. McCaffrey and Henry can only drag so much, and Week 7 projects 98 against CJ.

copies.headline: CJ's 4-2 Is Doing Heavy Lifting
copies.body: CJ is 4-2 with a 37-29 all-play, which is honest enough — 117.2 a game, 6th of 12, nothing fraudulent about it. The problem is forward-facing. His roster projects to 106 a week, 12th of 12, which means the engine is Tyler Shough at quarterback and a Rashee Rice question mark. The last three weeks — 114.6, 112.4, 125.5 — are fine, stable, unspectacular, and propped up by +0.6 luck wins. The draft graded 83, 8th of 12. Week 7 projects 114 against Leif. Enjoy the record while it lasts.

copies.headline: 4-2 Built On Fumes And Favorable Matchups
copies.body: Peter's 4-2 looks fine until you open the hood: 666.4 points for, 8th of 12, an all-play of 28-38 that says this is a 42% team wearing a winning record. The 606.9 against is the fewest in the league, and his luck sits at +1.5 wins, 2nd-highest. Then the last three weeks: 163.0, 95.4, 69.8. That's a nosedive, not a trend line. The draft was the best in the league at 89, and the roster still projects 124 a week, 4th of 12. Lamar and Bijan are there. The scores aren't.

copies.headline: 3-3 Is The Scoreboard Lying
copies.body: Grant is 3-3 because the schedule has been gentle — 610.7 points against, 2nd-fewest in the league — not because he's scored. His 107.9 per game ranks 9th of 12, and the all-play record is 26-40, a 39% clip that's also 9th. The +0.6 luck is the whole story. Last three weeks: 104.4, 121.3, 105.5, which is 12-21 all-play. The roster isn't the problem — Amon-Ra St. Brown, Zay Flowers and Christian Watson project 129 against Christian in Week 7. Start converting that projection into actual Sunday points.

copies.headline: Kaleb's 4-2 Is A Beautiful Lie
copies.body: Kaleb is 4-2 and that's the only nice number here. The all-play is 24-42, 36%, 10th of 12 — over the last three weeks it's 6-27, 18%, dead last in the league — and he's +1.8 wins above expected, the luckiest mark of anyone. He's scoring 105.5 a game and getting outscored by his own record. The 86 draft grade was legitimately good, T-4th, but Goff, Jeanty and Drake London project to 118 against Mitchell, which is fine, not scary. The 2023 title was won differently. Regression is patient.

copies.headline: Mitchell's Roster Keeps Writing Checks Nobody Cashes
copies.body: Mitchell is 1-5 with the 7th-best scoring average in the league, which is the kind of sentence that makes a man stare at a wall. The 27-39 all-play says he's been roughly average; the -1.5 luck says average hasn't been rewarded. But the last three weeks — 102.5, 132.9, 85.5, a 9-24 all-play — are no longer bad luck, they're just bad. Jahmyr Gibbs and Nico Collins still project this thing to 124 a week, 5th in the league. Week 7 against Kaleb, the excuses run out.

copies.headline: Noah's October Pulse Is Faint But Real
copies.body: Noah drafted well — 86 out of 100, T-4th in the league — and has spent six weeks proving a draft grade is not a lineup. 101.6 a week, 11th of 12, a 20-46 all-play, and a luck figure of -0.8 that refuses to give him an excuse: he hasn't been robbed, he's been outscored. The last three weeks (110.5, 141.3, 108.5, 54% all-play) are genuinely encouraging. Drake Maye and Garrett Wilson are real. The problem is 113 projected weekly, 10th of 12, and 105 against Peter. The postseason assassin needs a postseason first.

copies.headline: Ja'Marr Chase Deserves Better Than This
copies.body: Isaac is averaging 99.8 a week, 12th of 12, and an all-play record of 17-49 means he's beaten 26% of the league's lineups all year. The 2-4 record is actually generous — he's plus-0.5 wins over expected. Week 6's 79.0 was a new season low and the third straight loss. The strange part: this roster projects for 122 a week, 7th of 12, with Chase, Nabers, Stroud and Saquon on it. That's a lineup problem or a luck problem, not a talent problem. Week 7 projects 128 against Logan. Fix it there.

intro: Adam is 6-0 with a 150.9 per-game average and an 89% all-play, which is the polite way of saying he's beaten the other eleven of you roughly nine times out of ten without needing a single favor from the schedule. At the other end, Isaac's 34.4 is actually behind Noah's 35.0 by six tenths, and he earns it with a 99.8 average and a 26% all-play — last place by production, not by bad beats. Logan is the week's big riser, #10 to #4 on a 76% form rating that's third-best on the board despite a 2-4 record and a luck figure of -1.5. Peter went the other way, #3 to #7, because a 36% form reading and a 42% all-play were always going to catch up to a 4-2 record built on +1.5 luck.
